question: Should memory-core expose scoped dreaming as per-agent agents.list[].dreaming, as a plugin-level dreaming.agents allowlist, or defer new config in favor of runtime pressure/backoff behavior?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the public config location and schedule scope are compatibility-sensitive product/API choices that affect strict schema, docs, upgrade expectations, and the two open implementation paths.

options.title: Accept scoped enablement first
options.body: Land a narrow schema-backed opt-out or allowlist for which agents are included in dreaming, and split per-agent schedules or staggering into a separate design if still needed.

options.title: Require full scheduling design
options.body: Keep both open PRs paused until per-agent schedules, stagger semantics, and precedence are designed together.

options.title: Avoid new config for now
options.body: Close or pause scoped-config work and rely on pressure/backoff fixes for OOM mitigation, leaving per-agent opt-out unsupported.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped enablement first
recommendation.body: Land a narrow schema-backed opt-out or allowlist for which agents are included in dreaming, and split per-agent schedules or staggering into a separate design if still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core dreaming and config-adjacent history makes this the best available owner for the API-shape decision.
